en: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra entitled "Dependent Origination.

At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling among the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven upon a stone slab as white as a pale woolen blanket, together with great śrāvakas such as Jitāśva; with bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas adorned with the jewels of immeasurable virtues, such as the noble Maitreya, Avalokiteśvara, and Vajrapāṇi; and with gods such as Mahābrahmā, Sahāmpati, Nārāyaṇa, Maheśvara, and Śakra.
Together with Indra, the lord of the gods, and Pañcaśikha, the king of the gandharvas,

the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara then rose from his seat, draped his upper robe over one shoulder, and resting his right knee upon the summit of Mount Meru, he bowed with palms joined toward the Blessed One and addressed the Blessed One as follows:

“O Blessed One, these deities, who adorn the worship of the caityas and have entered this circle of the assembly, somehow have produced the merit of the holy life; yet in this world with its gods, Māras, and Brahmās, among this generation of recluses and brahmins, monks and nuns, laymen and laywomen, they produce far more abundant merit than the Blessed One’s teaching of the Dharma— thus do they entreat the Blessed One.”

Then the Blessed One spoke to them this verse on dependent origination: "Of those phenomena that arise from a cause, the Tathāgata has declared their cause, as well as their cessation; thus is the teaching of the Great Śramaṇa."
Avalokiteśvara, this dependent origination is the Dharma-body of the Tathāgatas;
whoever sees dependent origination sees the Tathāgata.

And whichever son of good family or daughter of good family, endowed with faith, constructs on an unoccupied spot of ground a shrine the size of an *āmalaka* fruit, a Bodhi tree the size of a needle, and a parasol the size of a *bakula* flower, and recites the verse on the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) of dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), produces Brahma-merit.
Having passed away from here and met his death, he is reborn in the Brahma-world;
then, having passed away from there and met his death, he is reborn in the fellowship of the Śuddhāvāsa deities.
Thus spoke the Blessed One; and all those śrāvakas and those bodhisattva mahāsattvas [rejoiced].
including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra titled "Dependent Origination" (Ārya-pratītyasamutpāda).
